title: The Peat Bog
text: A bog of good black peat, the kind that burns all winter, has been cut in old steps by spades long rotted. The surface quivers when you stand on it. Bogs keep what falls into them, the old cutters said, and never give it back whole.

options.label: Cut peat from the old steps; it burns all winter, and the House will be glad of it.

outcomes.text: The work is heavy and wet. Once a spade strikes something soft, and nobody digs there again.

options.label: The sharpest searches the black water for what the bog keeps.

outcomes.text: An old sword lies in the peat, still gripped by a hand gone brown as leather. The fingers do not want to let go.

options.label: Leave the bog be; what it keeps, it keeps.

outcomes.text: On the way out the bog takes the Leader's leg to the knee. They pull free, but the greave stays behind.
